renderingModel.observation: public CustomEvents (search, diagnostic, dataLoadingConfigError), the public API return values (completeDataRequest results), and the detached state snapshots from getDataLoadingState()
renderingModel.driving: public methods (updateConfig, startDataLoading, completeDataRequest, getDataLoadingState), the public search input (part="input") value + input event, and connect via appendChild

jsdomTests: emits dataLoadingConfigError with structured issues when the dataLoading candidate is invalid
invokes onDataLoadingConfigError callback with the same detail object emitted on the event
deduplicates identical invalid candidates but re-emits after a valid config resets the signature
does not emit dataLoadingConfigError for a valid dataLoading update
API-032.observable: updateConfig({dataLoading:{protocol:'bogus'}}) emits exactly one public `dataLoadingConfigError` CustomEvent whose detail is {issues:[{path:'protocol',code:'invalid-value',message:...}]}; the onDataLoadingConfigError callback receives the SAME detail reference as the event; a repeated identical invalid candidate emits nothing; an intervening valid dataLoading update resets the dedup signature so the same invalid candidate re-emits; a valid update emits no config error
positivePaths: invalid candidate -> exactly one dataLoadingConfigError event with issues[0] {path:'protocol', code:'invalid-value'}
callback invoked once with the same detail object reference as the event
negativePaths: identical invalid candidate repeated -> NO second emission (deduplicated by signature)
API-032.dedupBoundary: Dedup distinguishes a repeated (signature-identical) invalid candidate from a genuine new invalid state: emitting the same invalid candidate twice yields exactly one event; a valid update resets the dedup state so the same invalid candidate emits again afterwards.
API-032.distinctionFromBroaderInvalidConfig: This contract is scoped to the `dataLoading` candidate only. The verification drives invalid `dataLoading` explicitly (protocol:'bogus'); it does not assert on unrelated legacy-config validation paths, so the characterized boundary is the data-loading config-error channel.

jsdomTests: defers the initial search until connected when startDataLoading is called before mounting
emits exactly one initial search when startDataLoading is called repeatedly after connect
is a no-op for the legacy protocol and leaves idle state
emits a search request observable through both the event and the state snapshot
API-060.observable: calling startDataLoading() before appendChild does NOT emit a search; the first public `search` event fires only after the element is connected; repeated startDataLoading() calls after connect emit exactly ONE `search` (idempotent); the emitted search is observable both as the `search` event detail.request and as getDataLoadingState().activeRequest (matching requestId + queryGeneration, status 'loading', busy true); for legacy protocol startDataLoading is a no-op and the state stays idle
positivePaths: start before connect -> 0 search -> appendChild -> exactly 1 search; activeRequest.requestId matches the event request
start after connect x3 -> exactly 1 search (idempotent repeated start)
active request observable via BOTH the public search event AND getDataLoadingState (separate boundaries asserted separately)
negativePaths: startDataLoading with legacy protocol -> 0 search; state idle, busy false, activeRequest null
API-060.boundariesSeparated: Public start() and async projection are separate boundaries: repeated-start idempotence is driven purely by the public search event count and the state snapshot, and deliberately does NOT infer internal scheduling from a final snapshot alone.

jsdomTests: reports an idle snapshot before startDataLoading is called
reports an active snapshot while a request is outstanding and a completed snapshot after acceptance
returns detached snapshots so mutating one does not affect internal state
API-061.observable: before startDataLoading: status 'idle', busy false, activeRequest null, error null; while a request is outstanding: status 'loading' with activeRequest matching the emitted request; after a matching completion is accepted: projectionPending true synchronously then, after a microtask/task flush, status settles (busy false, activeRequest null); the returned snapshot is detached — mutating a returned activeRequest.position.page or status does NOT affect a subsequent getDataLoadingState() call
positivePaths: idle snapshot before start (status idle, activeRequest null)
completed snapshot after acceptance settles asynchronously (busy false, activeRequest null)
negativePaths: mutation of a returned snapshot (position.page=999, status='tampered') does not leak into a fresh snapshot
API-061.classificationNote: Existing preserved. Per the Lead directive API-061 was already classified Existing. This task preserves that classification while adding an explicit public detached-snapshot mutation-safety test and idle/active/completed snapshot coverage; no reclassification was warranted.

jsdomTests: returns "unknown-request" for an unrecognized requestId and does not mutate state
returns "stale" when completing a superseded request after a newer search advances the generation
accepts a matching completion synchronously while projecting the result asynchronously
returns "resource-limit" and emits a diagnostic for an oversized cursor token
returns "invalid" without projecting items for an unrecognized status
without an acknowledged coordinator validates shape and returns invalid/unknown-request only
API-062.observable: completeDataRequest returns a synchronous DataRequestCompletionResult: 'invalid' for malformed envelopes and unrecognized completion status; 'unknown-request' for an unrecognized requestId (and state/DOM unchanged); 'stale' when the active request was superseded by a newer search that advanced queryGeneration; 'accepted' for a matching completion — projectionPending true synchronously then settles asynchronously (e.g. 'exhausted' status after flush); 'resource-limit' for an oversized cursor token with a public `diagnostic` event (name 'acknowledgedDataLoadingResourceLimit', detail.reason 'cursor-token-size') and getDataLoadingState().resourceLimit populated; without a coordinator (legacy) it validates shape and returns only 'invalid'/'unknown-request'
positivePaths: accepted matching completion -> synchronous 'accepted' + projectionPending true -> async settle
resource-limit via oversized cursor token -> 'resource-limit' + diagnostic event + state.resourceLimit.reason 'cursor-token-size'
stale via a newer search superseding the active request -> 'stale'
negativePaths: unknown requestId -> 'unknown-request' AND no state mutation (status/activeRequest unchanged) AND no option-node DOM change
unrecognized status ('bogus') -> 'invalid' AND no option-node DOM change
API-062.syncAcceptanceVsAsyncProjection: Synchronous acceptance is classified by the RETURN value (~'accepted'), whereas async projection is observed separately via projectionPending then the settled snapshot. A returned 'accepted' is explicitly NOT treated as DOM projection: the test asserts projectionPending true immediately after acceptance and settlement only after a flush. Negative paths verify both the return classification AND the absence of unintended state/DOM mutation (not just the returned string).
API-062.resourceLimitScope: Cursor resource-limits are exercised only via public config + completion: paginationMode:'cursor' config plus a completion returning an oversized nextCursor produces a public 'resource-limit' return, a public `diagnostic` event, and a populated state.resourceLimit — so the resource-limit path IS publicly observable without private access; no gap remained for this branch.

notes: API-062 negative paths assert both the return classification AND the absence of unintended state/DOM mutation (state snapshot unchanged, option-node count unchanged), not merely the returned string.
API-062 distinguishes synchronous acceptance (return value) from asynchronous projection (projectionPending -> settled snapshot); a returned 'accepted' is not treated as DOM projection.

The resource-limit branch (cursor-token-size) is reachable via public config + completion (paginationMode:'cursor' plus an oversized nextCursor), so it is characterized without private access; no observability gap remains for it.
The 'stale' result is produced through a purely public path: a second search typed into input[part="input"] advances queryGeneration, making the first request's completion classify as 'stale'.
API-060 tests the public start() boundary (search-event count + state snapshot) separately from async projection, avoiding inference of internal scheduling from a final snapshot alone.

Chromium was conditionally authorized but not added: the four contracts are method-result/event-payload/state-snapshot surfaces fully observable under jsdom; no real rendering/scroll/trust/animation is involved.
